questions.question: What is the standard equation for a line passing through a point (x0, y0) with slope m?
questions.explanation: The lecturer explicitly states that any line through a point has the equation y - y0 = m(x - x0).
questions.flashcard_front: What is the equation for a line through (x0, y0) with slope m?
questions.flashcard_explanation: This is the standard point-slope form of a linear equation used to define the tangent line.

questions.question: In calculus, the slope m of the tangent line at x0 is called the derivative of f, denoted f'(x0).
questions.explanation: The lecturer defines the slope m of the tangent line as f'(x0), the derivative of f.
questions.flashcard_front: What is the slope of the tangent line to y = f(x) at x0?
questions.flashcard_back: The derivative of f at x0, denoted f'(x0).
questions.flashcard_explanation: The derivative represents the instantaneous slope of the function at a specific point.

questions.question: How is the tangent line defined in relation to secant lines?
questions.answer: The tangent line is the limit of the secant lines PQ as the point Q approaches the fixed point P.
questions.explanation: The lecturer defines the tangent line as the limit of secant lines PQ as Q tends to P.
questions.flashcard_front: How is the tangent line defined using secant lines?
questions.flashcard_back: It is the limit of secant lines PQ as Q approaches P.
questions.flashcard_explanation: This limit process allows us to calculate the slope of the tangent line analytically.

questions.question: Given a function y = f(x), what is the y-coordinate of the point P at x0?
questions.explanation: The lecturer states that to specify point P given x0, the y-level is f(x0).
questions.flashcard_front: What is the y-coordinate of point P on the curve y = f(x) at x0?
questions.flashcard_explanation: The y-coordinate is simply the function evaluated at the given x-value.
